who: Chandogya Upanishad IV.4-9 · tr. F. Max Müller, 1879
quote: His teacher gave Satyakama ‘four hundred lean and weak cows’. ‘I shall not return unless I bring back a thousand,’ he said. And he did.
meaning: He kept going for years, until 400 weak cows became 1,000.

who: Yi Hwang (Toegye) · Twelve Songs of Dosan, song 9, 1565 · tr. from Korean
quote: Though I cannot see them, the road they walked lies before me. The road they walked lies before me: how can I not walk it?
meaning: The old masters are gone, but their road is here. So I walk it.

quote: The master leads you to the door; the practice is up to you.

who: Mau Piailug and his student Nainoa Thompson · Hawai'i, 1979
quote: Mau: ‘Can you see the island?’ Nainoa: ‘I cannot see the island but I can see an image of the island in my mind.’ Mau: ‘Good. Don't ever lose that image or you will be lost.’
meaning: Hold the picture of where you are going, and you won't get lost.

who: Shiva Samhita 3.18 · tr. Srisa Chandra Vasu, 1914
quote: The first condition of success is the firm belief that it (vidya) must succeed and be fruitful; the second condition is having faith in it; the third is respect towards the Guru...
meaning: First, believe the method works. Then trust it. Then respect your teacher.

who: Vyasa, commentary on Yoga Sutra 1.20 · tr. J. H. Woods, 1914
quote: Belief ... like a good mother, it protects the yogin. For him [thus] believing ... there is the further (upa) attainment of energy.
meaning: Trust in the path protects you like a mother. Then energy comes.

who: Shu-ha-ri, stages of learning in Japanese arts · Kotobank · tr. from Japanese
quote: Shu: keep your teacher's form until it is truly yours. Ha: learn from others and grow. Ri: leave and create something new.
meaning: First copy your teacher exactly. Then grow. Only then make something new.

who: Bhagavad Gita 2.40 · tr. Annie Besant, 1922 ed.
quote: In this there is no loss of effort, nor is there transgression. Even a little of this knowledge protects from great fear.
meaning: No effort on this road is wasted. Even a little guards you from fear.

who: Plutarch · Progress in Virtue 15, tr. F. C. Babbitt, 1927
quote: ...the thought and recollection of good men... gives support to those who are making progress... and in all difficulties keeps them upright and saves them from falling.
meaning: Remembering good people helps you stay standing when things get hard.

who: Ralph Waldo Emerson · The Conduct of Life, 1860
quote: Our chief want in life, is, somebody who shall make us do what we can. This is the service of a friend.
meaning: What we need most is someone who makes us do what we can.
